You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 Zombicide 2nd Edition Zombicide: 2nd Edition brings the modern classic of cooperative zombie survival back to the table with faster, smoother, and more cinematic gameplay! Released in 2021, this new edition of the smash-hit Zombicide builds on the original game’s legacy of over-the-top zombie slaying, teamwork, and escalating chaos. Players take on the roles of everyday Survivors fighting together in a city overrun by the undead. The Zombies are controlled by the game itself, forcing the group to coordinate their movement, manage noise, search for weapons and equipment, and take bold risks as the horde grows more dangerous. This edition refines the original Zombicide experience with streamlined rules, updated ranged attack priority, simplified door interactions, improved vehicle rules, and a new Dark Zone system that lets zombies lurk unseen until the survivors get too close. Across 25 missions, players will scavenge, level up, unlock powerful gear, and fight their way through the infected streets in a desperate struggle for survival and explosive zombie-slaying action! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Game Mechanics 2.1 Zones 2.2 Survivors 2.2.1 Survivor Skills 2.3 Equipment 2.4 Adrenaline Points (AP) and Danger Level 2.5 Zombies 3 Gameplay 3.1 Player Turn 3.2 Zombie Turn 4 Game End Overview Zombicide is a cooperative game in which players move around a map, complete mission objectives, and escape without dying or being overwhelmed by Zombies. Each mission has its own win condition, shown in the top right. Game Mechanics Zones The board/map consists of square Zones that are either outside or inside. Inside a building, a Zone is a room. On a street, a Zone is the area between crosswalk markings and/or building walls (or the board's edge). Survivors have line-of-sight in any non-diagonal direction to any other street Zones up to the board's edge as long as they aren't blocked. However, a Survivor can only see as far as one Zone into a building with an open door (and must be directly adjacent to the Zone). From an inside Zone, a Survivor can only see as far as one Zone to any adjacent room through an open door, but can see into the street with no limit. Survivors Unless the mission states otherwise, players take control of six Survivor characters (players may control more than one, depending on the number of players). Adults have 3 HP and kids (identified by a yellow emoji icon have 2 HP. Kids have 1 less HP than adults, but start with the Slippery skill (ignore Zombies when moving, do not spend extra actions). (Click the yellow triangle on the right side of a character card to see definitions for their skills.) Survivor Skills Ambidextrous : All weapons are treated as if they had the Dual symbol . Charge : Move up to 2 Zones to a Zone containing at least 1 Zombie. Entering a Zone containing Zombies ends the Move Action. Free action. Can only be used once per turn. Jump : Move 2 Zones, ignoring everything except walls and closed doors. Costs 1 action. Can only be used once per turn. Ignores movement-related skills (like +1 Zone or Slippery). Lucky : For each action, you may re-roll all dice once. Matching Set : If you find a weapon with the Dual symbol , you immediately receive a second card of the same type. Medic : You and all Survivors in the same Zone may heal 1 HP. You earn 1 AP per wound healed this way. Free action. Can only be used at the end of a round. Shove : All Zombies standing in the Survivor's Zone are pushed to an adjacent Zone chosen by you. Free Action. Can only be used once per turn. Slippery : The Survivor ignores Zombies when performing Move Actions and does not spend extra Actions when performing a Move Action out of a Zone with Zombies.
